title: How to Create a Power BI Dashboard
description: Build a simple interactive Power BI dashboard from a structured dataset.
prerequisites: A sample Excel or CSV dataset
permissions: No special enterprise permissions are required for a local report.
steps: Import your Excel or CSV data using Get Data.
Review data types and remove obvious data-quality issues in Power Query.
Create relationships between tables when a model contains multiple tables.
Add cards, charts, tables, and slicers to the report canvas.
Publish the report to the Power BI Service when you are ready to share it.
result: A report page with interactive visuals, filters, and a clear KPI layout.
troubleshooting: If visuals are blank, check data types, relationships, filters, and whether the source contains rows.
mistakes: Adding too many visuals to one page.

title: How to Refresh Power BI Data
description: Understand manual and scheduled refresh options for Power BI reports.
prerequisites: A Power BI report connected to a data source
permissions: The required permissions depend on the workspace and data source.
steps: Open the report or semantic model and identify its data source.
Refresh in Power BI Desktop to validate the query locally.
Publish the updated model if required.
In Power BI Service, configure credentials and refresh settings.
Run a manual refresh and review refresh history.
result: The dataset reflects current source data and refresh history shows a successful run.
troubleshooting: For failed service refreshes, inspect credentials, gateway connectivity, source availability, and query errors.
mistakes: Assuming Desktop refresh guarantees Service refresh.
Changing source paths without updating the model.

title: How to Create a Salesforce Dashboard
description: Create a dashboard from reports and arrange useful sales or service KPIs.
prerequisites: Access to Salesforce reports and dashboards
permissions: Dashboard and report permissions vary by Salesforce edition and profile.
steps: Open the Dashboards area and select New Dashboard.
Choose a folder where the dashboard can be stored.
Add components based on existing reports.
Configure chart types and grouping to match the KPI.
Save and test filters and dashboard visibility.
result: A dashboard containing clear, role-appropriate business metrics.
troubleshooting: If a component is empty, verify the source report, filters, sharing settings, and permissions.

title: How to Create a Jira Workflow
description: Plan and configure a simple issue workflow for a project team.
prerequisites: Jira project administration access where workflow changes are permitted
permissions: Workflow administration requires appropriate Jira permissions.
steps: Map the desired statuses and transitions before editing Jira.
Open workflow administration and create or edit a workflow.
Add statuses and transitions that match the process.
Add conditions, validators, or post-functions only when necessary.
Publish or associate the workflow according to your Jira configuration.
result: Issues can move through a predictable lifecycle with appropriate controls.
troubleshooting: If a transition is missing, check workflow association, conditions, and project configuration.
mistakes: Adding complex automation before validating the basic workflow.
Changing shared workflows without impact analysis.

title: How to Create an Azure Storage Account
description: Create a storage account and review the core configuration choices.
permissions: The exact role required depends on the subscription and resource group policy.
steps: Open the Azure portal and choose Create a resource.
Select Storage account and choose the subscription and resource group.
Configure region, performance, redundancy, and security settings.
Review networking and data-protection options.
Validate the configuration and create the resource.
result: A storage account is available for approved storage workloads.
troubleshooting: If deployment fails, inspect subscription limits, policy assignments, naming rules, and permissions.
mistakes: Selecting redundancy without understanding cost and availability needs.

title: How to Connect Snowflake to Power BI
description: Connect a Snowflake data source to Power BI and validate the connection.
prerequisites: Network access to the Snowflake environment
permissions: Snowflake privileges must allow the required database/schema access.
steps: Confirm the Snowflake warehouse, database, and schema details.
In Power BI Desktop, choose the Snowflake connector.
Enter the server and warehouse information.
Authenticate using the approved enterprise method.
Select tables or use a query and validate a small sample before modeling.
result: Power BI can retrieve approved Snowflake data for analysis.
troubleshooting: Check network restrictions, credentials, warehouse availability, role privileges, and connector versions.
mistakes: Using a role without required privileges.
Pulling an unnecessarily large dataset during testing.

title: How to Fix Microsoft Teams Microphone Problems
description: Troubleshoot common Teams microphone issues on desktop systems.
permissions: Operating-system microphone permissions may be required.
steps: Check the selected microphone in Teams settings.
Confirm the operating system allows Teams to access the microphone.
Test the microphone in another application.
Restart Teams after changing permissions or device selection.
If using a managed device, check organizational audio policies.
result: Teams detects the intended microphone and meeting participants can hear audio.
troubleshooting: If another application works but Teams does not, focus on Teams device selection, permissions, updates, and policy.
mistakes: Testing with a muted hardware headset.

title: How to Create an IAM Role in AWS
description: Create an AWS IAM role using least-privilege principles.
prerequisites: A clear workload or service requirement
permissions: IAM administration permissions are required to create or modify roles.
steps: Define the trusted entity that needs to assume the role.
Create a narrowly scoped permission policy.
Create the role and attach the approved policy.
Review the trust policy and permissions boundary if applicable.
Test access with a non-production workload before broader rollout.
result: A role grants only the access required by the intended workload.
troubleshooting: Access denied errors require checking identity policies, resource policies, trust relationships, boundaries, and explicit denies.
